units.leftText: Paul, an apostle — sent not from men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead —
units.rightText: Paul, an apostle (not from men, neither through man, but through Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead),

units.leftText: and all the brothers with me, To the churches of Galatia:
units.rightText: and all the brethren that are with me, unto the churches of Galatia:

units.leftText: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: Grace to you and peace from God the Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ,
leftNotes: 1:3 SBL, BYZ, and TR God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ

units.leftText: who gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
units.rightText: who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us out of this present evil world, according to the will of our God and Father:

units.leftText: to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen. No Other Gospel
units.rightText: to whom be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.leftText: I am amazed how quickly you are deserting the One who called you by the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel —
units.rightText: I marvel that ye are so quickly removing from him that called you in the grace of Christ unto a different gospel;

units.leftText: which is not even a gospel. Evidently some people are troubling you and trying to distort the gospel of Christ.
units.rightText: which is not another gospel: only there are some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.

units.leftText: But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be under a curse!
units.rightText: But though we, or an angel from heaven, should preach unto you any gospel other than that which we preached unto you, let him be anathema.

units.leftText: As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be under a curse! Paul Preaches the Gospel
units.rightText: As we have said before, so say I now again, If any man preacheth unto you any gospel other than that which ye received, let him be anathema.

units.leftText: Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
units.rightText: For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? or am I striving to please men? if I were still pleasing men, I should not be a servant of Christ.

units.leftText: For I want you to know, brothers, that the gospel I preached was not devised by man.
units.rightText: For I make known to you, brethren, as touching the gospel which was preached by me, that it is not after man.

units.leftText: I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it; rather, I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For neither did I receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but it came to me through revelation of Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.
units.rightText: For ye have heard of my manner of life in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and made havoc of it:

units.leftText: I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries and was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
units.rightText: and I advanced in the Jews’ religion beyond many of mine own age among my countrymen, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.

units.leftText: But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by His grace, was pleased
units.rightText: But when it was the good pleasure of God, who separated me, even from my mother’s womb, and called me through his grace,

units.leftText: to reveal His Son in me so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood,
units.rightText: to reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the Gentiles; straightway I conferred not with flesh and blood:

units.leftText: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the apostles who came before me, but I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.
units.rightText: neither went I up to Jerusalem to them that were apostles before me: but I went away into Arabia; and again I returned unto Damascus.

units.leftText: Only after three years did I go up to Jerusalem to confer with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
units.rightText: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas, and tarried with him fifteen days.

units.leftText: But I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.
units.rightText: But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.

units.leftText: I assure you before God that what I am writing to you is no lie.
units.rightText: Now touching the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.

units.leftText: Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
units.rightText: Then I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.

units.leftText: I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
units.rightText: And I was still unknown by face unto the churches of Judæa which were in Christ:

units.leftText: They only heard the account: “The man who formerly persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.”
units.rightText: but they only heard say, He that once persecuted us now preacheth the faith of which he once made havoc;

units.leftText: And they glorified God because of me.
units.rightText: and they glorified God in me.

units.leftText: Fourteen years later I went up again to Jerusalem, accompanied by Barnabas. I took Titus along also.
units.rightText: Then after the space of fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also with me.

units.leftText: I went in response to a revelation and set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders, for fear that I was running or had already run in vain.
units.rightText: And I went up by revelation; and I laid before them the gospel which I preach among the Gentiles but privately before them who were of repute, lest by any means I should be running, or had run, in vain.

units.leftText: Yet not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.
units.rightText: But not even Titus who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:

units.leftText: This issue arose because some false brothers had come in under false pretenses to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.
units.rightText: and that because of the false brethren privily brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:

units.leftText: We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.
units.rightText: to whom we gave place in the way of subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.

units.leftText: But as for the highly esteemed— whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism — those leaders added nothing to me.
units.rightText: But from those who were reputed to be somewhat (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth not man’s person)—they, I say, who were of repute imparted nothing to me:
leftNotes: 2:6 Literally God does not accept the face of man

units.leftText: On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted to preach the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised.
units.rightText: but contrariwise, when they saw that I had been intrusted with the gospel of the uncircumcision, even as Peter with the gospel of the circumcision

units.leftText: For the One who was at work in Peter’s apostleship to the circumcised was also at work in my apostleship to the Gentiles.
units.rightText: (for he that wrought for Peter unto the apostleship of the circumcision wrought for me also unto the Gentiles);

units.leftText: And recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John — those reputed to be pillars — gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
units.rightText: and when they perceived the grace that was given unto me, James and Cephas and John, they who were reputed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, that we should go unto the Gentiles, and they unto the circumcision;
leftNotes: 2:9 That is, Peter; also in verses 11 and 14

units.leftText: They only asked us to remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do. Paul Confronts Cephas
units.rightText: only they would that we should remember the poor; which very thing I was also zealous to do.

units.leftText: When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.
units.rightText: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I resisted him to the face, because he stood condemned.

units.leftText: For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, for fear of those in the circumcision group.
units.rightText: For before that certain came from James, he ate with the Gentiles; but when they came, he drew back and separated himself, fearing them that were of the circumcision.

units.leftText: The other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.
units.rightText: And the rest of the Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that even Barnabas was carried away with their dissimulation.

units.leftText: When I saw that they were not walking in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”
units.rightText: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Cephas before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest as do the Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, how compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?
leftNotes: 2:14 Some translators close this quotation after verse 16 or 21.

units.leftText: We who are Jews by birth and not Gentile “sinners”
units.rightText: We being Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

units.leftText: know that a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ. So we, too, have believed in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.
units.rightText: yet knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we believed on Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ, and not by the works of the law: because by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.

units.leftText: But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin? Certainly not!
units.rightText: But if, while we sought to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also were found sinners, is Christ a minister of sin? God forbid.

units.leftText: If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I prove myself to be a lawbreaker.
units.rightText: For if I build up again those things which I destroyed, I prove myself a transgressor.

units.leftText: For through the law I died to the law so that I might live to God.
units.rightText: For I through the law died unto the law, that I might live unto God.

units.leftText: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.
units.rightText: I have been crucified with Christ; and it is no longer I that live, but Christ liveth in me: and that life which I now live in the flesh I live in faith, the faith which is in the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself up for me.

units.leftText: I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.
units.rightText: I do not make void the grace of God: for if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nought.

units.leftText: O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your very eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified.
units.rightText: O foolish Galatians, who did bewitch you, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was openly set forth crucified?

units.leftText: I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith?
units.rightText: This only would I learn from you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

units.leftText: Are you so foolish? After starting in the Spirit, are you now finishing in the flesh?
units.rightText: Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now perfected in the flesh?

units.leftText: Have you suffered so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing?
units.rightText: Did ye suffer so many things in vain? if it be indeed in vain.

units.leftText: Does God lavish His Spirit on you and work miracles among you because you practice the law, or because you hear and believe?
units.rightText: He therefore that supplieth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?

units.leftText: So also, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
units.rightText: Even as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned unto him for righteousness.

units.leftText: Understand, then, that those who have faith are sons of Abraham.
units.rightText: Know therefore that they that are of faith, the same are sons of Abraham.

units.leftText: The Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and foretold the gospel to Abraham: “All nations will be blessed through you.”
units.rightText: And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all the nations be blessed.

units.leftText: So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith. Christ Has Redeemed Us
units.rightText: So then they that are of faith are blessed with the faithful Abraham.

units.leftText: All who rely on works of the law are under a curse. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law.”
units.rightText: For as many as are of the works of the law are under a curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one who continueth not in all things that are written in the book of the law, to do them.

units.leftText: Now it is clear that no one is justified before God by the law, because, “The righteous will live by faith.”
units.rightText: Now that no man is justified by the law before God, is evident: for, The righteous shall live by faith;

units.leftText: The law, however, is not based on faith; on the contrary, “The man who does these things will live by them.”
units.rightText: and the law is not of faith; but, He that doeth them shall live in them.

units.leftText: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”
units.rightText: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us; for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:

units.leftText: He redeemed us in order that the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit. The Purpose of the Law (Romans 7:1–6|ROM 7:1-6*)
units.rightText: that upon the Gentiles might come the blessing of Abraham in Christ Jesus; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

units.leftText: Brothers, let me put this in human terms. Even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.
units.rightText: Brethren, I speak after the manner of men: Though it be but a man’s covenant, yet when it hath been confirmed, no one maketh it void, or addeth thereto.

units.leftText: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.
units.rightText: Now to Abraham were the promises spoken, and to his seed. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.

units.leftText: What I mean is this: The law that came 430 years later does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.
units.rightText: Now this I say: A covenant confirmed beforehand by God, the law, which came four hundred and thirty years after, doth not disannul, so as to make the promise of none effect.

units.leftText: For if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise; but God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.
units.rightText: For if the inheritance is of the law, it is no more of promise: but God hath granted it to Abraham by promise.

units.leftText: Why then was the law given? It was added because of transgressions, until the arrival of the seed to whom the promise referred. It was administered through angels by a mediator.
units.rightText: What then is the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise hath been made; and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.

units.leftText: A mediator is unnecessary, however, for only one party; but God is one.
units.rightText: Now a mediator is not a mediator of one; but God is one.

units.leftText: Is the law, then, opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would certainly have come from the law.
units.rightText: Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could make alive, verily righteousness would have been of the law.

units.leftText: But the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin, so that by faith in Jesus Christ the promise might be given to those who believe.
units.rightText: But the scripture shut up all things under sin, that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.

units.leftText: Before this faith came, we were held in custody under the law, locked up until faith should be revealed.
units.rightText: But before faith came, we were kept in ward under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.

units.leftText: So the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
units.rightText: So that the law is become our tutor to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.

units.leftText: Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian. Sons through Faith in Christ
units.rightText: But now that faith is come, we are no longer under a tutor.

units.leftText: You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: For ye are all sons of God, through faith, in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
units.rightText: For as many of you as were baptized into Christ did put on Christ.

units.leftText: There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: There can be neither Jew nor Greek, there can be neither bond nor free, there can be no male and female; for ye all are one man in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.
units.rightText: And if ye are Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, heirs according to promise.

units.leftText: What I am saying is that as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, although he is the owner of everything.
units.rightText: But I say that so long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a bondservant though he is lord of all;

units.leftText: He is subject to guardians and trustees until the date set by his father.
units.rightText: but is under guardians and stewards until the day appointed of the father.

units.leftText: So also, when we were children, we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world.
units.rightText: So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the rudiments of the world:
leftNotes: 4:3 Or elemental forces; similarly in verse 9

units.leftText: But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
units.rightText: but when the fulness of the time came, God sent forth his Son, born of a woman, born under the law,

units.leftText: to redeem those under the law, that we might receive our adoption as sons.
units.rightText: that he might redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.

units.leftText: And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”
units.rightText: And because ye are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father.

units.leftText: So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God. Paul’s Concern for the Galatians
units.rightText: So that thou art no longer a bondservant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir through God.

units.leftText: Formerly, when you did not know God, you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods.
units.rightText: Howbeit at that time, not knowing God, ye were in bondage to them that by nature are no gods:

units.leftText: But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles? Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again?
units.rightText: but now that ye have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, how turn ye back again to the weak and beggarly rudiments, whereunto ye desire to be in bondage over again?

units.leftText: You are observing special days and months and seasons and years!
units.rightText: Ye observe days, and months, and seasons, and years.

units.leftText: I fear for you, that my efforts for you may have been in vain.
units.rightText: I am afraid of you, lest by any means I have bestowed labor upon you in vain.

units.leftText: I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you. You have done me no wrong.
units.rightText: I beseech you, brethren, become as I am, for I also am become as ye are. Ye did me no wrong:

units.leftText: You know that it was because of an illness that I first preached the gospel to you.
units.rightText: but ye know that because of an infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you the first time:

units.leftText: And although my illness was a trial to you, you did not despise or reject me. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God, as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.
units.rightText: and that which was a temptation to you in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but ye received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: What then has become of your blessing? For I can testify that, if it were possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
units.rightText: Where then is that gratulation of yourselves? for I bear you witness, that, if possible, ye would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.

units.leftText: Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?
units.rightText: So then am I become your enemy, by telling you the truth?

units.leftText: Those people are zealous for you, but not in a good way. Instead, they want to isolate you from us, so that you may be zealous for them.
units.rightText: They zealously seek you in no good way; nay, they desire to shut you out, that ye may seek them.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, it is good to be zealous if it serves a noble purpose — at any time, and not only when I am with you.
units.rightText: But it is good to be zealously sought in a good matter at all times, and not only when I am present with you.

units.leftText: My children, for whom I am again in the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you,
units.rightText: My little children, of whom I am again in travail until Christ be formed in you—

units.leftText: how I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you. Hagar and Sarah (Genesis 21:9–21|GEN 21:9-21*)
units.rightText: but I could wish to be present with you now, and to change my tone; for I am perplexed about you.

units.leftText: Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not understand what the law says?
units.rightText: Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?

units.leftText: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman.
units.rightText: For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, one by the handmaid, and one by the freewoman.

units.leftText: His son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, but his son by the free woman was born through the promise.
units.rightText: Howbeit the son by the handmaid is born after the flesh; but the son by the freewoman is born through promise.

units.leftText: These things serve as illustrations, for the women represent two covenants. One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery: This is Hagar.
units.rightText: Which things contain an allegory: for these women are two covenants; one from mount Sinai, bearing children unto bondage, which is Hagar.

units.leftText: Now Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem, because she is in slavery with her children.
units.rightText: Now this Hagar is mount Sinai in Arabia and answereth to the Jerusalem that now is: for she is in bondage with her children.

units.leftText: But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
units.rightText: But the Jerusalem that is above is free, which is our mother.

units.leftText: For it is written: “Rejoice, O barren woman, who bears no children; break forth and cry aloud, you who have never travailed; because more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband.”
units.rightText: For it is written, Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not; Break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: For more are the children of the desolate than of her that hath the husband.

units.leftText: Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise.
units.rightText: Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are children of promise.

units.leftText: At that time, however, the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit. It is the same now.
units.rightText: But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit, so also it is now.

units.leftText: But what does the Scripture say? “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with the free woman’s son.”
units.rightText: Howbeit what saith the scripture? Cast out the handmaid and her son: for the son of the handmaid shall not inherit with the son of the freewoman.

units.leftText: Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.
units.rightText: Wherefore, brethren, we are not children of a handmaid, but of the freewoman.

units.leftText: It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.
units.rightText: For freedom did Christ set us free: stand fast therefore, and be not entangled again in a yoke of bondage.

units.leftText: Take notice: I, Paul, tell you that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all.
units.rightText: Behold, I Paul say unto you, that, if ye receive circumcision, Christ will profit you nothing.

units.leftText: Again I testify to every man who gets himself circumcised that he is obligated to obey the whole law.
units.rightText: Yea, I testify again to every man that receiveth circumcision, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.

units.leftText: You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.
units.rightText: Ye are severed from Christ, ye who would be justified by the law; ye are fallen away from grace.

units.leftText: But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.
units.rightText: For we through the Spirit by faith wait for the hope of righteousness.

units.leftText: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value. What matters is faith expressing itself through love.
units.rightText: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth anything, nor uncircumcision; but faith working through love.

units.leftText: You were running so well. Who has obstructed you from obeying the truth?
units.rightText: Ye were running well; who hindered you that ye should not obey the truth?

units.leftText: Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.
units.rightText: This persuasion came not of him that calleth you.

units.leftText: A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.
units.rightText: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.

units.leftText: I am confident in the Lord that you will take no other view. The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
units.rightText: I have confidence to you-ward in the Lord, that ye will be none otherwise minded: but he that troubleth you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be.

units.leftText: Now, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the offense of the cross has been abolished.
units.rightText: But I, brethren, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? then hath the stumbling-block of the cross been done away.

units.leftText: As for those who are agitating you, I wish they would proceed to emasculate themselves!
units.rightText: I would that they that unsettle you would even go beyond circumcision.

units.leftText: For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh. Rather, serve one another in love.
units.rightText: For ye, brethren, were called for freedom; only use not your freedom for an occasion to the flesh, but through love be servants one to another.

units.leftText: The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
units.rightText: For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, even in this: Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.

units.leftText: But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another. Walking by the Spirit (Ezekiel 36:16–38|EZK 36:16-38*; Romans 8:9–11|ROM 8:9-11*)
units.rightText: But if ye bite and devour one another, take heed that ye be not consumed one of another.

units.leftText: So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
units.rightText: But I say, Walk by the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

units.leftText: For the flesh craves what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh. They are opposed to each other, so that you do not do what you want.
units.rightText: For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; for these are contrary the one to the other; that ye may not do the things that ye would.

units.leftText: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.
units.rightText: But if ye are led by the Spirit, ye are not under the law.

units.leftText: The acts of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, and debauchery;
units.rightText: Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these: fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness,

units.leftText: idolatry and sorcery; hatred, discord, jealousy, and rage; rivalries, divisions, factions,
units.rightText: idolatry, sorcery, enmities, strife, jealousies, wraths, factions, divisions, parties,

units.leftText: and envy; drunkenness, orgies, and the like. I warn you, as I did before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
units.rightText: envyings, drunkenness, revellings, and such like; of which I forewarn you, even as I did forewarn you, that they who practise such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
units.rightText: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

units.leftText: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
units.rightText: meekness, self-control; against such there is no law.

units.leftText: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
units.rightText: And they that are of Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with the passions and the lusts thereof.

units.leftText: Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit.
units.rightText: If we live by the Spirit, by the Spirit let us also walk.

units.leftText: Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.
units.rightText: Let us not become vainglorious, provoking one another, envying one another.

units.leftText: Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.
units.rightText: Brethren, even if a man be overtaken in any trespass, ye who are spiritual, restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness; looking to thyself, lest thou also be tempted.

units.leftText: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
units.rightText: Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

units.leftText: If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
units.rightText: For if a man thinketh himself to be something when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself.

units.leftText: Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.
units.rightText: But let each man prove his own work, and then shall he have his glorying in regard of himself alone, and not of his neighbor.

units.leftText: For each one should carry his own load.
units.rightText: For each man shall bear his own burden.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word must share in all good things with his instructor.
units.rightText: But let him that is taught in the word communicate unto him that teacheth in all good things.

units.leftText: Do not be deceived: God is not to be mocked. Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.
units.rightText: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

units.leftText: The one who sows to please his flesh, from the flesh will reap destruction; but the one who sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life.
units.rightText: For he that soweth unto his own flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth unto the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap eternal life.

units.leftText: Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
units.rightText: And let us not be weary in well-doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.

units.leftText: Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to the family of faith. Final Warnings and Blessings
units.rightText: So then, as we have opportunity, let us work that which is good toward all men, and especially toward them that are of the household of the faith.

units.leftText: See what large letters I am using to write to you with my own hand!
units.rightText: See with how large letters I write unto you with mine own hand.

units.leftText: Those who want to make a good impression outwardly are trying to compel you to be circumcised. They only do this to avoid persecution for the cross of Christ.
units.rightText: As many as desire to make a fair show in the flesh, they compel you to be circumcised; only that they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.

units.leftText: For the circumcised do not even keep the law themselves, yet they want you to be circumcised that they may boast in your flesh.
units.rightText: For not even they who receive circumcision do themselves keep the law; but they desire to have you circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh.

units.leftText: But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
units.rightText: But far be it from me to glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world hath been crucified unto me, and I unto the world.

units.leftText: For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything. What counts is a new creation.
units.rightText: For neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature.

units.leftText: Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule, even to the Israel of God.
units.rightText: And as many as shall walk by this rule, peace be upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.

units.leftText: From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.
units.rightText: Henceforth let no man trouble me; for I bear branded on my body the marks of Jesus.

units.leftText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
units.rightText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brethren. Amen.
